description: Pareto Chart Convergent Business Technologies · Free · All features included Most of the problem usually sits in a handful of causes. A Pareto chart finds them: bars sorted largest first, a cumulative line climbing across them, and a threshold that separates the vital few worth acting on from the trivial many that are not. Power BI can draw the bars and the line, but it will not sort, accumulate, find the cut or tell you where it falls. This visual does all of it, and says in plain words how many categories reach your threshold, so the answer is on the chart rather than in your head. Key Capabilities The Cut, Found For You - Set any threshold, not just 80%. The chart marks where the cumulative line crosses it and calls out how many categories get you there Vital Few and Trivial Many - Colour the two groups separately so the split is visible at a glance, with your own labels for each Tail Grouping - Roll a long tail into a single Other bar past a category count you choose, keeping the chart readable without hiding the total Two Axes, Properly Aligned - A value axis for the bars and a percentage axis for the line, with display units, decimals and independent formatting Labels That Get Out of the Way - Show data labels for every bar, only the vital few, or only those that fit; category labels rotate automatically when space runs short Small Multiples & Interactivity - One Pareto…
